head: 60e76226e91d8a2648d8c1e9ccefa649288a7fb2
title: Stabilize raw-score subtraction and target dtypes in MarginMSE
body:
## Change

Compute teacher and student score differences in at least float32 before MarginMSE, then match the detached teacher margins to the prediction dtype. This applies to dense, inherited sparse, multi-vector and cross-encoder MarginMSE implementations while preserving float64 predictions.

Finite float16 raw teacher scores `[40000, -40000]` have a finite float32 margin, but their subtraction overflows before the current code reaches its dtype conversion. Ordinary half/bfloat16 teacher margins also trigger mixed-dtype MSE backward errors on PyTorch 2.6; float64 cross-encoder predictions have the corresponding problem when their targets are forced to float32. PyTorch 2.14 handles those mixed-dtype backward cases, but the early subtraction still overflows there.

This was identified through source analysis and reproduced with a locally constructed WordEmbeddings encoder's public training forward/backward. This change concerns signed regression margins and their MSE targets; it does not change KL teacher-probability computation or embedding-distillation projection behavior.

## Validation

The candidate is `60e76226` against exact base `9ac7fdb4`:

| CPU environment | New tests on unchanged base | Candidate and adjacent suites |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| [PyTorch 2.6.0](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43921700020/job/133490383483) | 23 failed, 42 passed | 225 passed, 6 skipped |
| [PyTorch 2.14.1](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43922894820/job/133494562607) | 4 failed, 61 passed | 225 passed, 6 skipped |

The independent float64 reference checks signed-margin losses and gradients across four teacher dtypes, both precomputed margins and raw scores, ordinary and large scores, and all four loss families. Tests also check target detachment and unchanged inputs. Existing multi-vector and cross-encoder loss suites are included; skips are the existing CPU-only environment exclusions. All pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

The initial 2.14 validation job stopped because its harness expected the 2.6 baseline failure count. The linked follow-up records the observed 2.14 baseline and completes candidate validation without changing the candidate or test tolerances.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped with investigation, implementation and regression tests.
